481 interview rounds, 321 companies.

01 — Time

22,165 minutes

That is 369 hours — 46 eight-hour working days, or more than nine full working weeks, spent answering questions about yourself. Enough time to have built a product twice over.

The shape of it. Three campaigns dominate: 2021–22 (175 rounds), a short sharp 2023 (58), and the current run that began in April 2025 (241 and counting). Between them sits 2024 — two rounds all year.

03 — The pivot

AI went from 0% to a third of the pipeline

A round counts as AI/ML if the role title names AI, ML, GenAI or agents, or if the hiring company is AI-first by product. The 2025–26 campaign is the first in which AI roles are a structural share rather than a curiosity.

The tell. 34% of this window is AI/ML work, against 17% across the full career. The pipeline has changed character, not just volume.
04 — Rhythm

Which months hire

Seven years of monthly totals, and the same data folded into a single calendar year. The pattern is consistent enough to plan around.

Read it as a planning signal. February–March and May–August carry 385 of the 481 rounds — 80% of everything. October through January is consistently thin.
05 — Conversion

The funnel

Rounds attended, narrowed down to what they actually produced.

The honest number. 18 final rounds out of 481 — roughly one final for every 26 rounds. That ratio has held steady across all seven years, which means the bottleneck has never been the closing; it has been getting into pipelines that go deep.
06 — Final rounds

Every final, from the start

Rounds explicitly labelled final, fitment, last round, HR discussion or on-site closing. Several other processes reached a comparable depth without the label — Cognium's three rounds and DevRev's four-round series among them.

07 — Repeat companies

Who called more than once

102 companies ran two or more rounds, and 38 ran three or more. Ten came back in a different year entirely — a second, separate process months or years after the first.

The returners. CityMall, Coheso AI, Geekster, GoKwik, ImageKit, Newton School, Raft.ai, Recro, Wipro, Writesonic all opened a fresh process after an earlier one ended. Writesonic spans 2023 to 2025; GoKwik spans 2022 to 2025. These are the warmest doors in the list.

10 — Method

How this was counted

Source. Google Calendar, Personal calendar, 10 May 2020 to 1 October 2026. Other connected calendars over this period hold cohort sessions and mentoring only.

Counted. Every scheduled round attended as a candidate — screenings, exploratory calls, technical and coding rounds, system design, culture fit, HR and final rounds, plus agency-mediated rounds through Uplers, TopHire, BarRaiser, Intervue, Recro, Mercor, SuccessPact and Careernet.

Not counted. Mock interviews given as a mentor on Coding Ninjas and Topmate, Topmate and Calendly mentorship calls, TBE and Pesto cohort sessions, HyperVerge Academy huddles, BarRaiser expert onboarding, Skillsoft and FinSoftAI work meetings, Rajniti standups, group webinars, unattended take-home assessments, offer discussions, and onboarding.

Domains. Assigned from the hiring company's primary product, not the role title. Staffing platforms are tagged as such only where the end client is unknown.

Minutes. Scheduled duration from the calendar block where recorded. For the April 2025 onward set, duration is inferred from round type — 30 minutes for screenings and intro calls, 60 for technical rounds, 75 for finals and on-sites. Treat the 369-hour total as accurate to within roughly ten percent.

AI classification. Role title contains AI, ML, GenAI or agentic, or the hiring company is AI-first by product.

Finals. Only rounds explicitly labelled as final, fitment, last round, closing HR discussion or on-site are counted. This undercounts: some processes ended at a de facto final without the wording.

Known gaps. Rounds arranged purely over phone or WhatsApp and never placed on the calendar do not appear here. The 2021 and 2022 totals are the most likely to be slightly understated for that reason.

Sachin Kumar Shukla · interview record 2020–2026 · updated 04 October 2026
